key_insight: The paper establishes non-asymptotic total variation error bounds for Schrödinger–Föllmer samplers: O(h|ln h|) with exact drift and O(h|ln h| + 1/M) with Monte Carlo drift.
engineering_relevance: These bounds guide time-step and Monte Carlo sample-budget choices for high-dimensional, multimodal sampling without relying on long-time ergodicity.
method: Derive Kolmogorov equation regularization estimates using the Bismut–Elworthy–Li formula.
Analyze total variation error through weak error estimates for non-smooth test functions.
Bound errors from time discretization and Monte Carlo drift approximation.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments illustrate convergence with respect to time-step size h and Monte Carlo sample size M, alongside sampler effectiveness.
watch_item: The rates require drift regularity assumptions; the improved 1/M dependence is compared with an earlier 1/√M bound in a different metric, L²-Wasserstein distance.
paper_title: Total variation error bounds for Schrödinger-Föllmer samplers
